{{Top}}
{{Quote|I had a dream I was a Jedi. I came back here and freed all the slaves.|Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
[[File:RodianFreeingEnslaved.png|thumb|right|250px|A [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] picking the lock on a cell in a slave den on the outskirts of [[Sclavos/Legends|Sclavos]]]]
'''Slavery''' was the practice wherein [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings were treated as property to be bought and sold, enforced by violence or other forms of coercion. It was typical for the owner of a slave to implant the slave with a device that would kill them if an escape attempt was made. In the more lawful portions of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] where slavery was allowed, if a slave was injured in a manner that devalued the slave or prevented him from performing his job by a third party, the owner was entitled to compensation from that third party for the depreciated value or the loss of the slave.

==History==
{{Quote|Talk about out of the frying pan&mdash;! Next to fallen Jedis, ''[sic]'' slavers are the most feared denizens of the galaxy&mdash;and they're also some of its lowest scum!|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="Star Wars (1977) 68">[[Star Wars (1977) 68|''Star Wars'' (1977) 68]]</ref>}}
[[File:Okeefe_dress.jpg|thumb|left|150px|[[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]] during her enslavement to [[Quintik Kahr]].]]
Before their collapse in [[25,200 BBY]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] used huge numbers of slaves for the building of their [[Star Forge]]. Their slaves included [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]],<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> [[Duros/Legends|Duros]], [[Human/Legends|Humans]], [[Drall/Legends|Drall]], and [[Selonian/Legends|Selonians]].<ref name="TEA" /> The [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] was built on slavery, which was an accepted practice through the empire.<ref name="Golden2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> Slavery was used by groups as disparate as [[Xim's empire]],<ref name="Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]],<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="Rise">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> the [[Ssi-ruuvi Imperium]],<ref name="Truce">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]], and the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. To chronicle the use of slavery by various civilizations over the history of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] was considered by many to be a futile task.

Slavery was made illegal by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] under the ''[[Rights of Sentience]]'' clause, but continued to exist, particularly in regions not under Republic control, primarily the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex sector]].<ref name="Cloak">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> On [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], some slaves were installed with [[Slave tracking device|chips]] that killed them if they tried to escape. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker]] had such chips installed within their bodies.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

For Anakin, who later trained as a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], his history as a slave created some difficult emotional complications for his prospect of life in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Because slavery naturally bred and intensified the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]-inducing emotions of hatred and fear—''anathema'' to the Jedi, as fostering these feelings was antithetical to the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi tenets]] and beliefs that strengthened their connection to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>—Anakin faced peculiar challenges of the mind and spirit in his quest not only to become a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]], but also to fulfill his destiny as "[[Chosen One/Legends|the Chosen One]]."<ref name="RP">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref><ref name="JQ:TST">''[[Jedi Quest: The Shadow Trap]]''</ref><ref name="JQ:TMOT">''[[Jedi Quest: The Moment of Truth]]''</ref> Anakin's advanced age for [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi initiation]] (at nearly 10 years old) combined with his native Tatooine background, compounded the emotional problems that arose as a result.<ref name="RP" /> Whenever Skywalker came into contact with anyone or anything that summoned to the present his or his mother Shmi's unsavory experience with slavery, the Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] was ever challenged to first acknowledge those feelings of hatred, anger or fear, allowing them to be felt, but then, critically, to let them pass, or "let them go," as was the Jedi way; Anakin was thus severely challenged on his early missions to [[Krayn]]'s Nar Shaddaa, [[Mission to Haariden|Haariden]], [[Mission to Mawan|Mawan]], [[Mission to Typha-Dor|Typha-Dor]], [[Mission to Romin|Romin]], and [[Mission to Fondor (Separatist Crisis)|Fondor]].<ref name="JQ:PTT">''[[Jedi Quest: Path to Truth]]''</ref><ref name="JQ:TMOD">''[[Jedi Quest: The Master of Disguise]]''</ref><ref name="JQ:TST" /><ref name="JQ:TMOT" /><ref name="JQ:TCOTG">''[[Jedi Quest: The Changing of the Guard]]''</ref><ref name="SWA1">''[[Star Wars Adventures 1: Hunt the Sun Runner]]''</ref><ref name="SWA2">''[[Star Wars Adventures 2: The Cavern of Screaming Skulls]]''</ref><ref name="SWA3">''[[Star Wars Adventures 3: The Hostage Princess]]''</ref> Young Skywalker felt acutely the sting of any injustice, as well, whenever he encountered it in his journeys throughout the galaxy. For example, when Anakin witnessed, in the Jedi mission to [[Romin]] in [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]], the stark disparity between the wealthy and the poor, the 17-year-old Padawan struggled with the intense feelings of disgust he felt for the injustices seen—clearly manifest both in the poorer areas of the planet's predominantly rich [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] and in the overwhelmingly bleak countryside hovel areas outside of [[Eliior|the city]]—the planet's [[Citizens' Resistance|citizenry]] was, in essence, enslaved to its [[Roy Teda|tyrant-dictator]]. Seeing the same severe injustices that he'd grown up with, Anakin had to concentrate to keep his breathing even: "''He had tasted [the injustice] in his mouth like the sand that filled the air of Tatooine. The hatred he felt was bred in his bones''."<ref name="JQ:TCOTG" />

The following year, in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], Skywalker continued to be vexed, but at greater intensities than ever before, by [[Skull Queen's fortress#Disturbing dreams|disturbing visions]] of darkness and distorted memories of his time as a slave.<ref name="SWA1" /><ref name="SWA3" /> He wished he could wipe from his mind his experience as a slave, and he grew increasingly worried about the safety of his mother, Shmi. It had been nine years—and many intervening interstellar [[Star Wars: Jedi Quest|missions]]<ref name="RP" /><ref name="Outbound">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref><ref name="Jedi Quest">[[Star Wars: Jedi Quest|''Jedi Quest'']]</ref>—since Anakin had promised her that he would become a Jedi Knight and return to Tatooine to free her, and he remained determined to keep that promise.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /><ref name="SWA2" /><ref name="SWA3" /> Fate would, however, tragically lead the 19-year-old Jedi back to his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] to find Shmi brutally held captive by [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]]. After Shmi died in his arms, young Skywalker took revenge on those who had taken his mother's life and killed off the whole tribe of Tusken Raiders in revenge.<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

[[File:Orvax_IV.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Slave Fair on [[Orvax IV]].]]
Unfortunately, after the rise of the Empire, slavery was once again given a degree of legitimacy with the issuance of [[Imperial Decree A-SL-4557.607.232]]. Citizens could now be enslaved as punishment for "crimes against the civil order".<ref name="TEA" /> Non-Humans and Human critics of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] alike were rounded up and enslaved en-masse for work on such projects as the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. In addition, early into the Empire's formation, the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] had been ordered by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to sell [[Nosaurian/Legends|Nosaurian]] women and children into a slave market at Orvax IV. The Empire's enforcer, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], learned of this during a debriefing for the [[Cleansing of New Plympto]] when Commander [[Vill]] let slip about the Emperor's order. Vader grew despondent enough at the revelation as a result that he abruptly ended his presence at the debriefing and could not fall asleep that night, due to remembering his own time as a slave. He later revealed what he had learned to the Emperor, and ultimately let it continue despite his misgivings after the Emperor told him the Imperial way was "different."<ref name="The Path to Nowhere">''[[Star Wars: Dark Times: The Path to Nowhere]]''</ref> [[Agorffi]],<ref name="GG9">''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]''</ref> [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]], [[Yuzzem]], and [[Talz/Legends|Talz]] were exploited for their strength while the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] and the [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] were used for their famous ship-building skills. Also the [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]], [[Chroman (species)|Chromans]], [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]] and [[Mustafarian/Legends|Mustafarians]] were enslaved for their mining skills, the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]] and [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] were enslaved for military operations and the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] and [[Kallidahin/Legends|Kallidahins]] for their cloning skills. Meanwhile, the Empire frequently ignored the trade of [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|girls]], who were enslaved for their beauty.<ref name="Hutt and Seek">{{StoryCite|story=Hutt and Seek|book=Tales from the New Republic}}</ref> Officially, however, regarding alien species such as Wookiees, those deemed to be non-sentient were not considered enslaved, but "domesticated."<ref name="HSCSSB">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] took a dim view of slavery and those worlds which fell under its sway tended to outlaw it. [[Vigo/Legends|Vigo]] [[Lonay]] reported to [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] a 53% decrease in slave revenues in his [[Sector/Legends|sector]] when several planets within it joined the Rebel Alliance and passed local laws forbidding the practice.<ref name="Shadows of the Empire">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

When the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] became the dominant galactic power, slavery was once again made illegal by [[New Republic Senate Resolution 54.325]].<ref name="Hutt and Seek" /> However, slavery still continued in remote areas of the galaxy particularly in the Outer Rim and on certain Imperial [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]] such as [[Byss/Legends|Byss]]. The former Imperial [[Procurator of Justice]] [[Hethrir]] was a major figure in the slave trade and sold undesirable captives into slavery at [[Crseih Station]] in the remote [[Crseih system/Legends|Crseih system]]. With his death (and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]'s identification of the other currently major galactic slave hub, [[Chalcedon/Legends|Chalcedon]]), the slave trade suffered a major blow.<ref name="Crystal Star">''[[The Crystal Star]]''</ref> Slavery re-emerged as a significant threat during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] as practiced by the [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong empire]]. In particular, the [[Chazrach]] slave race was used in military operations. However, this was short-lived, once they had been defeated.
[[File:Karazak_Slavers.jpg|thumb|left|224px|Karazak slavers]]
Slaving was often handled by experienced slaving guilds; three of the most notable were the [[Thalassian slavers/Legends|Thalassian slavers]], the [[Zygerrian Slavers Guild]], and the [[Karazak Slavers' Cooperative/Legends|Karazak Slavers Cooperative]].<ref name="Hutt and Seek" /> Other criminal groups such as the [[Exchange]] and the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] also had slave trades. The [[Invisible Market]] dealt largely with selling slaves on behalf of the [[Black market/Legends|black market]], especially since the black market was more out in the open.

In [[44 ABY]], due to the efforts of [[Freedom Flight]], [[The Perre Needmo Newshour]], and other groups, as well as the actions of several [[Lost Tribe of Sith|Lost Tribe Sith]] to desecrate the [[Fountain of Ancients]] on [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]], public support dramatically turned away from slavery. Most notably, the [[Chev]] species was freed from bondage to the [[Chevin/Legends|Chevin]], and the [[Treaty of Vontor]] was overturned, freeing the Nikto, [[Vodran (species)/Legends|Vodran]], and [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinians]] from Hutt bondage they had endured for the past 25,144 years.<ref name="Allies">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref> The galactic movement against slavery grew and soon, slaves all around the galaxy, from the [[Ssi-ruuk Star Cluster]] to the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], started to revolt against their masters. After the [[Blaudu Sextus revolt|violent repression of the revolt on Blaudu Sextus]], the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi Order]] decided to move in to support the movement against slavery, which led to all-out war between them and [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Natasi Daala]].

[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Krayt]] repealed many anti-slavery laws set in place after the fall of the Galactic Empire when he took control of the galaxy. He even enslaved the Mon Calamari species. Indentured servitude was also engaged in by crime lords who liked to appear more legitimate than their peers.<ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Droids and slavery==
{{Quote|You have an actual ''living slave''? <small>[fzzt]</small> How extravagant! We find droids ''far'' more efficient.''"<br />"''Oh, you'd be surprised what ''slaves'' can amount to sometimes&hellip; I once heard of one that became a ''Jedi Knight''.|A [[Unidentified Techno Union official 2|Techno Union official]] and a [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|disguised]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]|<ref name="Suited">{{TCWComicCite|6.10|Suited}}</ref>}}
[[File:R2D2-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|220px|Jawas often captured and sold droids that they found.]]
Another variation (at least to some) was ownership of droids. Some felt that this "ownership" was merely enslavement of their kind and fought to give them their freedom. An uprising of droids would later bring such ideas of their liberation into question.

Droids, including artificially intelligent droids, were typically treated as property. More advanced droids sometimes received proportionally more respect. Some protested the status of droids as slavery. This was a contentious issue, owing in part to the difficulty of assessing levels of [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial intelligence]], and determining which droids could be considered properly sentient. Although emancipation of droids was a radical concept, some opposed [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]] except for very simple droids.

Some droids enforced slavery alongside their organic companions.

The [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] considered higher level droids equal as fellow sentients. Under the Galactic Empire, no laws protected droids from abuse and those who showed them respect were looked upon as strange.

==Methods==
{{Quote|Any attempt to escape&hellip;''"<br />"''And they blow you up! BOOM!|Shmi Skywalker and her son, Anakin|<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />}}
[[File:Negotiating-DarkTimes3.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Chagrian and a Duros negotiating for a little Human slave girl.]]
Slavers had ways of keeping their charges on their leashes, literally and figuratively. The more physical means was attaching a chain to [[Shock collar/Legends|collars]] around their necks. The collar would be held by the slave's master, or attached to an object such as a wall.

Zygerrians used collars on their slaves which sent electric shocks through their bodies at the touch of a button. They also used [[Shock whip]]s.

Another method was placing transmitters inside their bodies. Any attempt to escape caused the transmitter to explode, killing the slave. However, this method had the drawback of resulting in the destruction of the slave and loss of property.

The [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] used the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] to enslave other beings, like [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] who enslaved the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]].

Despite all these possibilities, the most powerful method was likely psychological. Slaves would be made to feel that escape was impossible, and they would be forced to remain slaves. However, this method often failed, and slaves escaped fairly often.

==Image==
{{Quote|I&hellip; do not understand. Organics own droids. What is the utility of owning other ''organics''? What else can&hellip; ''slaves'' provide?''"<br />"''Simple &ndash; ''entertainment value''.|[[T1-LB]] and [[Jarael]], discussing slavery|<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic 40">[[Knights of the Old Republic 40|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 40]]</ref>}}
[[File:Slaves_on_demesel.jpg|thumb|Slavery on [[Demesel/Legends|Demesel]].]]
The most common of slaves were either workers or portrayed as entertainment. Worker slaves were forced to labor, while often receiving little food and water. They were the type more frequently seen, especially in governments and more legal slaving organizations.

Entertainment slaves were forced typically to wear revealing outfits to please their masters (or their master's guests) and submit to them. These were usually slaves to criminals, rather than major organizations. Notable examples included the Twi'lek [[Oola/Legends|Oola]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], who were enslaved by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]].<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Only those of us who have been slaves can really taste freedom.|14-year-old Anakin Skywalker.|<ref name="Jedi Quest: The Way of the Apprentice">''[[Jedi Quest: The Way of the Apprentice]]''</ref>}}
According to ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', the Empire outlawed slavery. Later sections of the book indicate that the Empire instituted slavery as a judicial punishment for certain ill-defined crimes.
